text: When a sacred political order treats its own survival as sacred under perceived existential threat, self-sacralization can legitimate sacrificial demand.
falsificationCriteria: Perceived existential threat does not increase self-sacralization or sacrificial demand in comparable cases.
Sacrificial demand appears without sacred-order self-preservation claims and is better explained by ordinary instrumental mobilization.
Anti-sacrificial or bounded-sacrifice cases cannot be distinguished from pathological sacrifice using the proposed variables.
